title: Design System: What Are We Watching

display.purpose: The SURPRISE ME key: wide black italic, 90s retail sign lettering; the only wide voice besides WHERE TO WATCH.

headline.purpose: Film title on the sleeve: black ultra-condensed caps.

title.purpose: Sign-board section plaques: yellow condensed caps on a 1px rule.

body.purpose: The film's one-line take on the sleeve insert, max 62ch.

print-label.purpose: Year, director and cast lines printed on the sleeve.

label.purpose: Board buttons, key labels and tags: condensed caps.

osd.purpose: VT323 on the tube and the VCR window only.

shadows.name: main-key
shadows.purpose: The big yellow key at rest.

shadows.name: main-key-pressed
shadows.purpose: The big yellow key pressed (3px travel).

shadows.name: key
shadows.purpose: The moulded sound key in the play bar.

shadows.name: watch-key
shadows.purpose: The sleeve's yellow WHERE TO WATCH key.

shadows.name: panel
shadows.purpose: Sign board resting on the counter; its only shadow.

shadows.name: recess
shadows.purpose: VFD window set into the play bar.

shadows.name: vfd-glow
shadows.purpose: text-shadow for VFD phosphor; the only UI glow.

shadows.name: highlight-overlay-scale
shadows.purpose: Highlight and hairline scale: VFD lip .06, vinyl sheen .07, poster edge .1, board hairline and case edge .12, sound key edge .14, board button hairline and wells .2, yellow key edges .5-.65, rewind seal edge .75.

shadows.name: shade-overlay-scale
shadows.purpose: Shade scale: lips .35, contact shadows .4-.6, case inner edge and hinge groove .65-.7, panel and key drops and VFD recess .8-.9.

shadows.name: bloom
shadows.purpose: three.js bloom on emissive surfaces: tube, VFD, neon; dropped on slow devices.

motion.name: channel-change
motion.purpose: Static between picks; 30% torn colour bars, else snow with CH 03.

motion.name: dial-detent
motion.value: 30deg per pick, exponential approach k=22/s with overshoot
motion.purpose: VHF dial turns one detent per channel change; instant when reduced.

motion.name: sleeve-settle
motion.value: opacity 340ms ease-out, transform 460ms ease-out (8px), blur 2px; force reveal 1400ms

motion.name: key-press
motion.purpose: Moulded key travel, 2-3px on press; board buttons do not travel.

motion.name: state-colour
motion.purpose: Board button (120ms) and key (150ms) colour and border changes.

motion.name: stage-fade
motion.purpose: Canvas fades in when the set is ready.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No transitions, sway, drift, hum, tracking tear or sleeve blur; dial jumps; render on change only.

components.name: Sign Board
components.description: The store's sign board printed flat: Counter Blue ground, white hairline, yellow condensed plaques on 1px rules.
components.html:
Decade

CLASSICS · CULT · DOCS · FRINGE · SPACE · 1138 FILMS

narrative.overview:
The page is a place, not a panel. A Blender-built silver 70s portable TV sits on a 90s VCR on a rental-store counter, lit in three.js in front of an out-of-focus Cycles plate of the store: face-out tapes on white shelving, blue section headers, a pink VIDEO and cyan OPEN LATE neon. The tube is the product's voice. The name WHAT ARE WE WATCHING lives on its VCR-blue idle screen, a pick is a channel change (half a second of snow or torn colour bars, one detent of the VHF dial, a static "shh"), and the film then plays on the tube like a tape.

Everything the hand touches sits in front of that scene and is made of the counter's own stuff: a sign board printed flat in counter blue with yellow plaques and flat blue buttons, a play bar of chunky moulded plastic keys with a VFD count window glowing cyan, and the back of a rental case (pebbled black clamshell over a printed insert under clear vinyl) that carries the film's words. Two worlds are composed and never blended: the lit 3D world behind, and the retail world of print and plastic in front. The owner rejected an earlier moulded, candy-coloured filter board as too "kid" (2026-09-27); the board is now printed flat like the sleeve, and moulded plastic is kept for the few keys that are actual hardware. The period line is pre-Frutiger-Aero: plastic, print and phosphor, never frosted glass or glossy bubbles.

Density is operational. The pick, the filters and the facts stay one glance away; the theatre happens on the tube, not by hiding controls.
keyCharacteristics: A lit 3D set (TV, VCR, counter, returned tapes) in front of a baked, bokeh'd store plate; one camera frames every layout.
Rental blue and sticker yellow carry the whole UI; VFD cyan and neon pink/cyan are light sources, not fills.
Archivo in two voices (wide black on the two yellow keys only, condensed caps everywhere else); VT323 only on the tube and the VCR.
Two surface grammars: play-bar and sleeve keys are moulded plastic that travels when pressed; the sign board is flat print with hairlines, blue buttons that turn yellow when chosen.
Every raster is procedural Blender output that carries its own provenance.

rules.name: The Light Source Rule
rules.body: Only things that emit light glow: the tube, the VFD, the neon. Glow (text-shadow, bloom) never lands on a panel, key or type that is paint or print.

rules.name: The Yellow Means Press Rule
rules.body: Among the controls, a Sticker Yellow surface means "this is the thing to press" or "this is chosen". Elsewhere yellow is signage and print: plaques and their rules, pinstripes, labels, the year and billing lines; never body copy.

rules.name: The Two Blues Rule
rules.body: Rental Blue is the store; VCR Blue is the tube. Do not swap them.

rules.name: The Tube Font Rule
rules.body: VT323 lives only on the tube (the OSD and idle screen canvases) and the VCR window. Anything printed or signed is Archivo.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Wide black is for the two yellow keys you press from across the room; condensed caps is print, read up close, and that includes the whole sign board. Reading text (the take, the actor field) is plain sentence-case Archivo. Do not invent a third display voice.

rules.name: The Moulded Plastic Rule
rules.body: Moulded plastic is for hardware keys only: the play bar (SURPRISE ME, sound) and the sleeve's WHERE TO WATCH. Each has a crisp inset top highlight, a crisp inset bottom lip and a soft blurred drop, and travels 2-3px down on press. Outer drop shadows are always blurred.

rules.name: The Flat Board Rule
rules.body: The sign board is printed flat like the sleeve (owner, 2026-09-27: the bubbly keys and fluorescent stickers read too "kid"). One flat Counter Blue ground, 1px hairlines, flat Rental Blue buttons that turn flat Sticker Yellow when chosen. No gradients, bevels, lips, press travel or candy colours on the board.

rules.name: The No Glass Rule
rules.body: No backdrop blur, no frosted or translucent panels. The only transparency is the clear vinyl sheen over the sleeve insert, a single faint diagonal band.

dos: **Do** keep the TV the first thing seen: centre on desktop, pinned across the top when stacked, with the yellow key directly under it.

**Do** make play-bar and sleeve keys moulded plastic (top highlight, bottom lip, soft drop, 2-3px travel), and keep the sign board flat: Rental Blue buttons with a white hairline, flat Sticker Yellow when chosen.
**Do** keep VT323 on the tube and the VCR only; wide black Archivo on the two yellow keys only, condensed caps for everything else.
**Do** put glow only on things that emit light: the tube, the VFD, the neon.
**Do** draw icons as SVG paths in the page and as canvas paths on the tube.
**Do** build new rasters in Blender, ship them beside index.html under the content hash, and embed their provenance.
**Do** evoke the era only: no real store's name, logo or marks.
donts: **Don't** use frosted glass, backdrop blur, glossy bubbles or any Frutiger-Aero finish.
**Don't** put a dark app card on a flat page; controls sit in the store world, on the counter.
**Don't** use hard, unblurred outer drop shadows; depth comes from the lit set and the moulded keys' inset lip and soft drop.
**Don't** set UI, signage or printed text in VT323.
**Don't** give a non-pressable control or panel a Sticker Yellow surface.
**Don't** bevel, mould or candy-colour the sign board: no gradients, lips, press travel or fluorescent fills on the board or its buttons.
**Don't** use text glyphs or emoji as icons.
